newsitem.title: USA: Appeals court affirms Time Warner ruling.
newsitem.headline: Appeals court affirms Time Warner ruling.

text.p: A federal appeals court Thursday upheld a preliminary injunction won by Time Warner Inc. that is keeping Rupert Murdoch's Fox News and Bloomberg Informational Television off a city-run cable television channel.

In November, U.S. District Judge Denise Cote ruled that the city had violated Time Warner's First Amendment rights under the U.S. Constitution by trying to force Time Warner to carry the Fox and Bloomberg programming and interfere with its editorial discretion.
Time Warner had argued that a cable system operator may prevent a city from placing on channels reserved to the city for educational or governmental purposes a 24-hour news or business news service.

The 2nd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed the lower court ruling on grounds that Time Warner had shown a probability of success of its claim that the city's planned use of educational and governmental channels would violate its franchise agreement with Time Warner.
The appeals court did not rule on the First Amendment issue.
Fox News is part of News Corp. Ltd.. Bloomberg Informational Television is part of privately held Bloomberg LP.
